content: Drospirenone has the potential to increase the levels or effects of various medications by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of these interactions is generally considered minor or unknown. Below are the specific interactions: 1. Drospirenone and Etoposide: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of etoposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 2. Drospirenone and Etravirine: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of etravirine through CYP3A4 modulation. 3. Drospirenone and Everolimus: Drospirenone could elevate the levels or effects of everolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 4. Drospirenone and Exemestane: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of exemestane via CYP3A4 interaction. 5. Drospirenone and Fedratinib: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of fedratinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 6. Felbamate and Ethinyl Estradiol: Felbamate decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. 7. Drospirenone and Felbamate: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of felbamate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 8. Drospirenone and Felodipine: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of felodipine via CYP3A4 modulation. 9. Ethinyl Estradiol and Frovatriptan: Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of frovatriptan by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. 10. Drospirenone and Fenofibrate: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fenofibrate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 11. Drospirenone and Fenofibrate Micronized: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of fenofibrate micronized through CYP3A4 interaction. 12. Drospirenone and Fenofibric Acid: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of fenofibric acid by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 13. Drospirenone and Fentanyl (all forms): Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) via CYP3A4 modulation. 14. Drospirenone and Finerinone: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of finerinone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 15. Drospirenone and Flibanserin: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of flibanserin through CYP3A4 interaction. 16. Drospirenone and Flunisolide (Inhaled): Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of inhaled flunisolide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 17. Drospirenone and Flurazepam: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of flurazepam via CYP3A4 modulation. 18. Drospirenone and Flutamide: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of flutamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 19. Drospirenone and Fluticasone Furoate: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate through CYP3A4 interaction. 20. Drospirenone and Fluticasone (Inhaled): Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of inhaled fluticasone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 21. Forskolin and Drospirenone: Forskolin may increase the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergy. 22. Drospirenone and Fosamprenavir: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 23. Drospirenone and Fosaprepitant: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of fosaprepitant via CYP3A4 modulation. 24. Drospirenone and Fostamatinib: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of fostamatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 25. Drospirenone and Gefitinib: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of gefitinib through CYP3A4 interaction. 26. Drospirenone and Glasdegib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of glasdegib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 27. Drospirenone and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via CYP3A4 modulation. 28. Goldenrod and Drospirenone: Goldenrod may increase the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergy. 29. Drospirenone and Guanfacine: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of guanfacine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 30. Drospirenone and Haloperidol: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of haloperidol through CYP3A4 interaction. 31. Drospirenone and Hydrocodone: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of hydrocodone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 32. Drospirenone and Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate via CYP3A4 modulation. 33. Drospirenone and Ibrutinib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of ibrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 34. Drospirenone and Idelalisib: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of idelalisib through CYP3A4 interaction. 35. Drospirenone and Ifosfamide: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ifosfamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 36. Drospirenone and Imatinib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of imatinib via CYP3A4 modulation. 37. Ethinyl Estradiol and Imipramine: Ethinyl estradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) like imipramine, potentially increasing serum concentrations and adverse effects. 38. Drospirenone and Indinavir: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of indinavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 39. Iodinated Glycerol and Drospirenone: This combination may decrease renal clearance, potentially leading to hyperkalemia. 40. Iodine and Drospirenone: Similar to iodinated glycerol, iodine may decrease renal clearance, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia. 41. Drospirenone and Irinotecan (all forms): Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of irinotecan and its liposomal form by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 42. Drospirenone and Isosorbide Dinitrate/Mononitrate: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of these medications via CYP3A4 modulation. 43. Drospirenone and Isradipine: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of isradipine through CYP3A4 interaction. 44. Drospirenone and Istradefylline: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of istradefylline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 45. Drospirenone and Itraconazole: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of itraconazole via CYP3A4 modulation. 46. Drospirenone and Ivacaftor: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of ivacaftor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. 47. Drospirenone and Ivosidenib: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of ivosidenib through CYP3A4 interaction. 48. Drospirenone and Ixabepilone: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ixabepilone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 49. Drospirenone and Ixazomib: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of ixazomib via CYP3A4 modulation. 50. Drospirenone and Ketamine: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of ketamine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. This list continues with similar interactions for other medications, where drospirenone generally increases the levels or effects of the drugs by modulating CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions remains uncertain in most cases.
